function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

I’m afraid I don’t have the ability to add events to your personal calendar or send you notifications automatically. However, here’s what you can do yourself: | Platform | How to Add | |----------|------------| | **Google Calendar** (desktop/mobile) | • Click “Create” → “Event”.
• Set title: *“Netflix Subscription Renewal”*.
• Date: March 27, [year].
• Time: choose when it matters (e.g., 9 AM).
• Under “Add notification”, pick “Email” or “Pop‑up” 10–15 minutes before. | | **Apple Calendar** (iOS/macOS) | • Tap “+” → “New Event”.
• Title & date as above.
• In “Alert”, select “At time of event” or “5 min early.” | | **Microsoft Outlook / Office 365** | • New Appointment → Subject: Netflix renewal.
• Start/End dates accordingly.
• Reminder field – e.g., 30 mins prior. | | **Todoist / Any task manager** | • Create new task titled “Renew Netflix subscription”.
• Due date: March 27.
• Enable due-date reminder. | If you’d prefer a quick script that writes a text file reminding you later, let me know! Otherwise just follow one of those steps and you’ll get a timely nudge.
message.reasoning:
The user wants to create a reminder/notification? They want to do something like schedule an event at March 27. We cannot actually set reminders; we could suggest how to use calendar app or write code snippet.
